hero.headline: Oil Prices Rise as US and Iran Exchange Strikes
hero.body:
Oil prices climbed after the United States and Iran traded fresh military strikes in the Persian Gulf region, jeopardizing diplomatic efforts to secure a ceasefire agreement. The latest round of confrontations has intensified concerns about regional stability and potential disruptions to global energy supplies.

The escalation began when US forces fired a Hellfire missile at a tanker attempting to break through an American blockade of the Strait of Hormuz. The US military's Central Command said it subsequently repelled Iranian counterattacks in the region and struck sites on Iran's Qeshm Island. In response, Iran's Islamic Revolutionary Guards Corps claimed it attacked the US Fifth Fleet headquarters in Bahrain using missiles and drones, though the US military denied sustaining significant damage.

The exchanges extended beyond direct US-Iran confrontations when Iranian drones struck Kuwait's main international airport, causing heavy damage and killing at least one person. Kuwait briefly shut down the airport following the attack. Iran characterized the strike as retaliation for the earlier US missile and drone operations.

These military actions underscore the lack of political progress in resolving the Middle East crisis, despite optimistic statements from US officials. Secretary of State Marco Rubio claimed during a Senate hearing that a deal with Tehran was within reach and that Iran had agreed to negotiate aspects of its nuclear program previously off limits.

Iranian Foreign Minister Abbas Araghchi responded by emphasizing that any ceasefire must apply across all fronts in the region, including Lebanon. He stated that violating the ceasefire on one front constitutes a violation of the entire agreement and held the US and Israel responsible for any consequences.

The strikes pushed crude oil markets higher as traders assessed potential threats to energy supplies in the Persian Gulf, one of the world's most critical regions for oil production and transit. Stock markets reflected the uncertainty, with the Dow falling more than 350 points as oil prices and bond yields increased. Multiple market reports indicated that the US-Iran tensions were driving oil higher and contributing to broader market declines.

Energy analysts noted that US crude oil inventories have posted their sixth consecutive weekly decline, with gasoline inventories falling at record pace. Some analysts warned that gasoline could face supply crunches similar to those affecting crude markets.

The extent of future price movements depends on whether the military confrontations continue escalating or if diplomatic efforts succeed in containing the situation. Any sustained disruption to shipping lanes or production facilities in the Gulf region typically triggers significant price increases as markets price in supply risks, with ripple effects across the broader economy affecting transportation costs, manufacturing inputs, and consumer prices.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes 10 percent tariff on Canada, Mexico, and EU
cards.teaser: The administration is proposing new tariffs on major trading partners over forced labor concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has proposed tariffs of 10-12.5 percent on approximately 60 trading partners, including Canada, Mexico, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Taiwan, and Australia. The administration justified the levies by citing alleged forced labor failures by these countries.

The EU responded swiftly to the proposal, asserting that the U.S. should honor a tariff agreement reached in July and cautioning that these new tariffs would violate the spirit of that deal. The tariff announcement represents Trump's latest effort to reinstate his trade policy following a February Supreme Court ruling that limited his tariff authority.

cards.headline: Trump says Israel complicating Iran peace negotiations
cards.teaser: President Trump confirmed he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "crazy" and said Israel is making peace talks with Iran more difficult.
cards.body:
President Trump publicly criticized Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu during a profanity-laden phone call, telling him to halt military operations in Lebanon. Trump expressed frustration that Israel's intensified offensive was undermining U.S. efforts to de-escalate regional tensions and pursue peace negotiations with Iran, which had threatened to suspend talks over the Israeli campaign.

Netanyahu responded that he and Trump have "tactical disagreements" but remain aligned on overall strategy regarding Iran. The tension reflects Trump's broader effort to extricate the U.S. from the conflict with Iran, though Israeli drone strikes and Hezbollah rocket launches continued even as the leaders negotiated.

cards.headline: Senate advances immigration funding bill after Trump reverses course
cards.teaser: The Senate prepared to move forward with a reconciliation bill to fund immigration agencies after President Trump backed away from proposed cuts.
cards.body:
The Senate is moving forward with a reconciliation bill to fund immigration agencies after President Trump changed his position on proposed budget cuts. Republicans had initially planned cuts to certain federal programs but reversed course following pushback.

The revised legislation no longer includes the cuts to Justice Department and other agencies that Trump had initially sought to eliminate. Senate Republicans proceeded with the immigration package after the president's retreat on the funding dispute.

cards.headline: Supreme Court allows Alabama to use Republican-drawn congressional map
cards.body:
The Supreme Court has ruled that Alabama can implement its 2023 congressional map, a decision that permits a Republican-friendly redistricting plan to move forward. The ruling marks a significant moment in voting rights law and has drawn sharp criticism from dissenting justices.

Justice Sonia Sotomayor issued a forceful dissent, stating that the ruling "debases the democratic process." The case centered on Alabama's congressional district boundaries, which civil rights groups had challenged as intentionally diluting minority voting power.

The decision transforms how federal courts will evaluate voting rights challenges following the Supreme Court's earlier decision in Louisiana v. Callais, which weakened a major provision of the Voting Rights Act. Legal observers have noted that this ruling could have far-reaching implications for how states draw congressional districts and how courts review those maps going forward.

The case has a lengthy history. Black voters sued Alabama in 2021, arguing that the state's congressional map diluted their voting influence. A federal court panel agreed and ordered the state to redraw the map. When Alabama's legislature passed the 2023 plan, the same court found it still diluted Black voters' influence and ultimately rejected it. A court-appointed special master then drew a map that included a second majority-Black district, which the Supreme Court upheld in 2023.

However, following the Louisiana v. Callais decision, Alabama moved to use the 2023 map again for the upcoming elections. The three-judge panel that reviewed this attempt included Judge Stanley Marcus of the U.S. Court of Appeals for the 11th Circuit, a Bill Clinton appointee, along with two Trump-appointed district court judges.

In rejecting Alabama's attempt to use the 2023 map, the panel wrote that "when the legislature enacted the 2023 plan, it made a calculated, purposeful decision to refuse to provide the remedy for discriminatory vote dilution." The judges concluded that the legislature "well knew that a plan without an additional Black-opportunity district would dilute Black Alabamians' opportunity to participate in the political process, and it intentionally enacted that very plan."

The ruling signals that maps drawn with an intent to discriminate can still be challenged, even after the Louisiana v. Callais decision weakened voting rights protections. Alabama's Attorney General Steve Marshall said he would appeal the decision to the Supreme Court, stating that he was "not at all surprised" by the ruling but confident the state would ultimately prevail.

The Davin Rosborough, deputy director of the voting rights project at the American Civil Liberties Union, which represented some of the plaintiffs, emphasized the historical context of voter suppression in the South and the importance of Black voters having fair representation.

cards.headline: Trump says he will nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
cards.body:
President Trump indicated Wednesday that he plans to make acting Attorney General Todd Blanche the permanent leader of the Justice Department, though he declined to provide a specific timeline for submitting the nomination to the Senate.

During an appearance on the podcast Pod Force One, Trump expressed confidence in Blanche's performance. "He's a very talented guy. Todd's doing a very good job at DOJ," Trump said when asked about making the position permanent. The president responded affirmatively when directly asked if Blanche would become attorney general, saying "I think he will."

Blanche has served as acting attorney general since Trump took office. Before joining the administration, he worked as a defense attorney and represented Trump in various legal matters. His appointment as a permanent attorney general would require Senate confirmation by the Republican-controlled Senate, which could facilitate the approval process.

The nomination comes as Blanche faces significant legal challenges related to his handling of documents under the Epstein Files Transparency Act. Investigative journalist Katie Phang filed a lawsuit in federal court Monday alleging that Blanche engaged in a "brazen, shocking, and ongoing violation" of the transparency law requiring the Department of Justice to release all government documents about Jeffrey Epstein, the late financier and convicted sex offender.

The lawsuit accuses Blanche of missing statutory deadlines for releasing documents, making improper or excessive redactions, failing to explain redactions as required by law, and withholding or retracting documents after they were released. Congress passed the transparency act in November with a December 19, 2025 deadline for full document release.

Blanche has defended the redactions as necessary to prevent inadvertent identification of Epstein's victims, many of whom are minors, and acknowledged that "mistakes are inevitable." However, critics including House Judiciary Committee Democratic ranking member Jamie Raskin said there were "tons of completely unnecessary redactions" alongside failures to redact victims' names.

The lawsuit seeks to have the court declare the Justice Department in violation of the law, order release of all required documents without unlawful redactions, and appoint an independent special master from outside the department to oversee future compliance.

Additionally, the Justice Department's Office of Inspector General announced last week that it was launching its own audit into the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

The legal action represents the latest enforcement effort for the transparency law, which was authored by Democratic California Representative Ro Khanna and Republican Kentucky Representative Thomas Massie. A hearing date for Phang's lawsuit has not yet been scheduled.

cards.headline: USAID shutdown linked to increased violence in Africa, study finds
cards.teaser: Research published in Science journal connects the dismantling of the development agency to sharp rises in armed clashes, protests, and riots across the continent.
cards.body:
New research suggests the shutdown of the U.S. Agency for International Development led to sharp increases in violence throughout Africa. A research paper published in the Science journal found that African countries that received the most support from USAID experienced armed clashes, protests, and riots in the months following the agency's dismantling.

The study examined patterns of violence in countries that had previously relied on USAID assistance. Areas that depended heavily on the agency's programs saw notable upticks in civil unrest and armed conflict after operations ceased.

hero.headline: Hotel fire in New Delhi kills at least 21
hero.teaser: A blaze at a hotel in India's capital killed at least 21 people and injured dozens more.
hero.body:
A fire at a hotel in New Delhi killed at least 21 people and injured dozens more, according to authorities. The blaze appears to be the deadliest in the Indian capital in at least four years.

Authorities are investigating the cause of the fire. The scale of casualties and the number of injured suggest the fire spread rapidly through the building.

cards.headline: Ukraine strikes St. Petersburg as Putin economic forum begins
cards.teaser: Ukraine targeted military and oil facilities near Russia's second-largest city on the opening day of an annual economic conference.
cards.body:
Ukrainian drones struck oil storage facilities near St. Petersburg as Putin's economic forum opened in the city. President Volodymyr Zelensky publicly confirmed Ukraine's responsibility for the attack, which set an oil terminal ablaze.

The strikes targeted the region containing Russia's second-largest city and coincided with the first day of the marquee economic event. Putin is scheduled to address the forum in the coming days.

cards.headline: Four sentenced to death for attack on Nigerian church
cards.teaser: A court sentenced four men to death for killing worshippers at a Catholic church in Nigeria.
cards.body:
Four men received death sentences for killing worshippers at a Catholic church in Nigeria. A fifth man was discharged and acquitted due to insufficient evidence against him.

The court handed down the sentences after finding the four guilty of the deadly attack on the place of worship. The attack had targeted congregants during a service at the Catholic church.

cards.headline: Trump administration proposes 10 percent tariff on Canada, Mexico, and EU
cards.teaser: The administration is proposing new tariffs on major trading partners over forced labor concerns.
cards.body:
The Trump administration has proposed tariffs of 10-12.5 percent on approximately 60 trading partners, including Canada, Mexico, the European Union, the United Kingdom, Taiwan, and Australia. The administration justified the levies by citing alleged forced labor failures by these countries.

The EU responded swiftly to the proposal, asserting that the U.S. should honor a tariff agreement reached in July and cautioning that these new tariffs would violate the spirit of that deal. The tariff announcement represents Trump's latest effort to reinstate his trade policy following a February Supreme Court ruling that limited his tariff authority.

cards.headline: Drone strike kills eight on bus in Russian-occupied Ukraine
cards.teaser: A bus was hit by a drone in the eastern Donetsk region, according to an official.
cards.body:
A drone strike on a bus in Ukraine's eastern Donetsk region killed eight people, according to an official. The bus was traveling through the Russian-occupied territory when it was hit.

The attack is part of the broader conflict in eastern Ukraine, where casualties continue to mount from ongoing military operations in the region.

cards.headline: FBI shoots man dead after hostage situation at California bank
cards.teaser: A man who took hostages at a bank was shot and killed by the FBI after a standoff.
cards.body:
An armed man took hostages at a California bank, leading to a standoff with FBI agents. The situation unfolded over two days, with two hostages released on Tuesday. The remaining hostages were freed the following day unharmed.

FBI agents shot and killed the suspect, ending the standoff. All hostages survived the incident without injury.

cards.headline: CBS News fires 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley
cards.teaser: The veteran journalist was dismissed after confronting leadership at a staff meeting.
cards.body:
CBS News fired 60 Minutes correspondent Scott Pelley on Tuesday following a clash with the network's new management at a staff meeting. During the confrontation, Pelley accused leadership of "murdering" the news show.

After his dismissal, Pelley issued a public statement accusing CBS executives of silencing employees and instructing him to "inject falsehoods and bias" into his reporting. He claimed the network pushed unverified claims and gave politicians input on interviews. Pelley noted that 60 Minutes had remained the top-rated program in America for decades because of its integrity and quality.

cards.headline: FBI kills hostage-taker after standoff at California bank
cards.teaser: FBI agents shot and killed a man who took multiple hostages at a Chase Bank building in Bakersfield after a standoff that stretched into a second day.
cards.body: FBI agents fatally shot a man who had taken hostages at a California bank building in Bakersfield. The incident unfolded over two days, with two hostages released on Tuesday. The remaining hostages were freed on Wednesday when the standoff ended. Police confirmed that all hostages were released safely without injury.

cards.teaser: President Trump confirmed he called Israeli Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu "crazy" and said Israel is making peace talks with Iran more difficult.

The revised legislation no longer includes the cuts to Justice Department and other agencies that Trump had initially sought to eliminate. Senate Republicans proceeded with the immigration package after the president's retreat on the funding dispute.

cards.headline: Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass advances to November runoff
cards.teaser: Mayor Karen Bass will face a second challenger in November as Spencer Pratt and Nithya Raman compete for the remaining spot in the runoff election.
cards.body:
Los Angeles Mayor Karen Bass won Tuesday's primary election but fell short of the 50% threshold needed to avoid a runoff. She will advance to November's general election as the top finisher.

Bass will face either former reality TV star Spencer Pratt or city council member Nithya Raman in the November runoff. With more than 60% of votes counted, Pratt held 30% of the vote while Raman secured 22%.

cards.headline: State Senator Scott Wiener to face Connie Chan in race for Pelosi's House seat
cards.teaser: California State Senator Scott Wiener and San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan will compete in November to succeed Nancy Pelosi in Congress.
cards.body:
State Senator Scott Wiener and San Francisco Supervisor Connie Chan have advanced to the general election for Nancy Pelosi's House seat, representing California's 11th Congressional District. The two emerged from a competitive primary field to face off in November.

The race will determine representation for one of the nation's most liberal districts. With Pelosi's departure, the contest has drawn significant attention as a key indicator of progressive politics in San Francisco and a competition to establish new leadership within the American left.

cards.headline: Former British intelligence chief Alex Younger dies at 62
cards.teaser: Sir Alex Younger, who led MI6 and served nearly three decades in British intelligence, has died.
cards.body: Sir Alex Younger, former chief of Britain's MI6 intelligence service, has died at age 62. He spent nearly three decades in British intelligence, joining the service in 1991 and eventually rising to lead the Secret Intelligence Service. He was knighted for his contributions to the country.

cards.headline: US Crude Oil Inventories Drop for Sixth Consecutive Week
cards.teaser: American crude oil stockpiles continued their decline as the nation's emergency oil reserve approached historic lows.
cards.body:
US crude oil inventories fell for the sixth consecutive week, according to the Energy Information Administration. The sustained drawdown has lowered overall stockpiles while gasoline inventories have also declined sharply, prompting concerns about potential supply constraints.

The Strategic Petroleum Reserve continues approaching historic lows despite earlier commitments to replenish reserves. Energy trading firm Vitol has cautioned that gasoline could emerge as the next petroleum product facing supply pressures as inventory levels drop across multiple categories.

cards.headline: Stock Markets Fall as Oil Prices and Bond Yields Rise
cards.teaser: The Dow Jones Industrial Average dropped 400 points as rising oil prices and increasing bond yields weighed on equities.
cards.body:
Major US stock indexes declined, with the Dow falling more than 350 points. The S&P 500 saw its nine-day winning streak come under threat while the Nasdaq also traded lower. Rising oil prices driven by Middle East tensions contributed to the market decline.

Bond yields crept higher during the session, adding to pressure on stock valuations. Investors assessed economic data including ADP employment figures and ISM manufacturing reports. The combination of energy price increases and rising yields created headwinds for equities across sectors.

cards.headline: Trump Administration Contests Court Order on Tariff Refunds
cards.teaser: The administration began repaying some tariff money after a court order but signaled it may restrict how businesses claim full refunds.
cards.body:
The Trump administration started processing refunds for certain tariffs following a court directive. However, officials indicated they may implement new measures that could make it harder for some businesses to receive the complete amounts they are owed.

The Supreme Court struck down many of the administration's previous tariffs in February. The legal battles over trade duties have left companies seeking reimbursement for payments made under policies the courts later invalidated.

cards.headline: US Announces New Tariffs Over Forced Labor Concerns
cards.teaser: The government imposed fresh tariffs citing forced labor issues, months after the Supreme Court invalidated earlier trade duties.
cards.body:
The United States has announced new tariffs on goods produced with forced labor, targeting dozens of countries including the UK. This announcement follows the Supreme Court's February decision that invalidated many tariffs imposed during the Trump administration.

The move reflects efforts to use trade policy as a tool to address labor rights concerns while working within the legal framework established by the court's recent ruling on presidential tariff authority.

cards.headline: Short Seller Andrew Left Convicted of Fraud
cards.teaser: A guilty verdict against prominent activist short seller Andrew Left is expected to reshape how investors publicly discuss their trading positions.
cards.body:
Andrew Left, a securities analyst and trader who appeared on CNBC and Fox Business, was convicted by a federal jury in California of securities fraud. He faced charges including one count of engaging in a securities fraud scheme, 17 counts of securities fraud, and one count of making false statements to federal investigators. As a short seller, Left profited by betting that stock prices would fall.

Left faces a maximum penalty of 25 years in prison. The conviction is expected to have significant implications for how activist short sellers operate, particularly regarding disclosure rules and public commentary about their positions.

cards.headline: Home Sellers Withdraw Listings at Fastest Rate Since 2020
cards.teaser: Homeowners are pulling properties off the market at near-record rates as buyers resist paying asking prices.
cards.body:
Sellers removed homes from the market at the highest pace since 2020, according to data from real estate brokerage Redfin. The surge in withdrawn listings reflects a standoff between sellers seeking higher prices and buyers unwilling to meet their demands.

Certain properties have languished unsold for months as the disconnect between buyer and seller expectations persists. Real estate agents attribute the extended time on market to pricing mismatches and broader economic uncertainty affecting housing demand.

hero.headline: Instagram alerts users targeted in AI chatbot hacking attacks
hero.body:
Instagram is notifying users whose accounts were compromised through a vulnerability in Meta's AI-powered support chatbot. The company confirmed that hackers exploited the system to gain unauthorized access to user accounts, with the breach affecting both high-profile and everyday users.

According to reporting from 404 Media, targets included Barack Obama's White House account, beauty retailer Sephora, and US Space Force Chief Master Sergeant John Bentivegna. Everyday users also reported similar account hijackings on Reddit and X over the weekend.

The attack exploited Meta's AI assistant, which was designed to help users with account issues including password resets. Videos shared on social media platforms showed hackers manipulating the chatbot into resetting targeted accounts. In one example, a hacker instructed Meta's AI assistant to link an account to a new email address. The bot sent a verification code to that email and allowed the hacker to reset the account password once they entered the correct numbers. In at least one case, a hacker used a virtual private network to spoof the account holder's location and bypass Meta's security safeguards.

Meta rolled out the AI support assistant globally on Facebook and Instagram earlier this year. According to a March press release, the feature could "take action for you on a growing set of requests directly within Facebook and in the future, on Instagram." The capabilities included reporting scams, removing impersonation accounts, and resetting passwords. The company described it as "a major step in our work to deliver stronger support on our apps."

Meta announced on Monday that the issue had been resolved and that it was "securing impacted accounts." However, the exact number of affected users remains unclear. Reports indicate that stolen account handles were listed for sale on the Telegram messaging platform.

Security researchers have identified the attack as a form of "prompt injection," in which attackers manipulate AI chatbots into carrying out malicious actions. Aiden Sinnott, a principal threat researcher at cybersecurity firm Sophos, warned that this category of attack will become increasingly common as companies deploy chatbots without adequate protections.

The incident raises broader concerns about using artificial intelligence for essential security functions like password management. As Meta increases its investment in AI technology, with founder Mark Zuckerberg directing a $145 billion spend on AI infrastructure this year, security vulnerabilities in these systems pose significant risks to users.

This breach adds to Meta's ongoing security challenges. The company continues to invest in two-factor authentication and other protective measures, but the AI chatbot vulnerability represents an emerging risk category as artificial intelligence becomes more integrated into core platform functions. Users are advised to enable all available security features and monitor their accounts for suspicious activity.

cards.headline: Google requires publishers to have option to opt out of AI search
cards.teaser: U.K. regulators are requiring Google to offer publishers a way to exclude their content from generative AI search features.
cards.body:
U.K. regulators have mandated that Google provide website publishers with a tool to opt out of generative AI search features. The Competition and Markets Authority argues this requirement strengthens publishers' positions when negotiating content deals with Google, addressing concerns about how their work is being used in AI-generated search results.

Google will first test the opt-out option in the U.K. before expanding it globally, giving publishers greater control over whether their content appears in AI-powered search features.

cards.headline: AI music startup Suno raises $400 million while facing copyright lawsuits
cards.teaser: The AI music generation company secured new funding despite ongoing legal challenges over its use of copyrighted material.
cards.body:
Suno, an AI music generation startup, has raised $400 million in new funding, valuing the company at over $5.4 billion. The funding round represents a significant jump from its previous $2.45 billion valuation about seven months earlier.

Despite ongoing copyright lawsuits challenging its AI music generation technology, the startup continues to attract investor backing. The substantial funding increase underscores investor confidence in the AI music generation sector and Suno's position as a leading platform in the space.

cards.headline: Amazon to display AI-generated product images in search results
cards.teaser: The retailer will use visual search and artificial intelligence to show computer-generated images matching user queries.
cards.body:
Amazon plans to show AI-generated product images in search results using visual search and artificial intelligence technology. These images will match customer search queries and help guide users toward relevant products available on the platform.

The feature represents Amazon's continued integration of AI into its shopping experience, building on previous implementations in product recommendations and customer service.

cards.headline: GitLab cuts 14% of workforce while scaling AI infrastructure
cards.teaser: The software development platform is reducing staff as it exits 22 countries and invests in handling AI workloads.
cards.body:
GitLab is cutting 14% of its workforce and exiting operations in 22 countries as part of a restructuring effort. The company is also reducing management layers to streamline operations.

The layoffs coincide with GitLab's push to scale its platform for AI workloads. The infrastructure investments aim to build the computational capacity needed to support artificial intelligence-related development work on its software development platform.

cards.headline: Google releases Fitbit Air blueprints for custom accessories
cards.teaser: The company shared CAD drawings and specifications allowing anyone to design and manufacture bands for the wearable device.
cards.body:
Google has released CAD drawings and technical specifications for its Fitbit Air device, allowing third-party manufacturers and individual makers to create custom bands and accessories. The blueprints include detailed measurements and guidelines for producing compatible products.

The release enables users to 3D print their own Fitbit Air accessories or design alternative band styles, including bicep bands. By making the specifications publicly available, Google is opening its wearable ecosystem to independent designers and manufacturers who can now create accessories without requiring official licensing agreements.

cards.headline: Microsoft announces new developments at Build 2026 conference
cards.teaser: The company unveiled Project Solara and other initiatives at its annual developer conference.
cards.body:
Microsoft held its Build 2026 conference with announcements targeting developers. The company unveiled Project Solara, a platform designed for devices running AI agents rather than traditional applications. Microsoft also announced advancements in quantum computing, revealing a new quantum chip that is 1,000 times more reliable than its predecessor.

AI chief Mustafa Suleyman discussed the competitive landscape of major AI labs during the keynote. Microsoft presented various tools and services aimed at developers working with artificial intelligence, along with updates to Windows as a development platform. The company projects it will have a quantum computer capable of solving commercially useful problems by the end of the decade.

hero.headline: Browns trade Myles Garrett to Rams in exchange for Jared Verse and draft picks
hero.body:
The Cleveland Browns traded star edge rusher Myles Garrett to the Los Angeles Rams on Monday in a blockbuster deal that brings younger defensive talent and future draft capital to Cleveland. The Rams sent linebacker Jared Verse and three draft picks to the Browns in exchange for the two-time NFL Defensive Player of the Year.

Garrett, 30, has been one of the league's premier pass rushers since the Browns selected him first overall in 2017. He holds the records for most sacks, pressures, and tackles for loss among all players since that draft year. In the 2025 season, he set a single-season sacks record with 23 and earned All-Pro recognition despite the Browns' disappointing 5-12 record and playoff miss.

The trade comes after months of uncertainty surrounding Garrett's future with the franchise. He requested a trade in 2024 following the team's 3-14 season, expressing a desire to play for a championship contender. Though the Browns signed him to a four-year, $160 million extension shortly after that request, which made him the highest-paid non-quarterback in league history at the time, Garrett's frustrations with the organization's direction lingered.

General manager Andrew Berry negotiated a contract restructuring with Garrett in March that deferred option payments across the 2026-28 seasons, allowing the trade to become financially feasible. Berry explained the decision to move on from their cornerstone player in a statement after the trade was announced.

"As discussions intensified we were stuck at a legitimate crossroads: do we hold on to a truly generational player who has become the identity of our team, or do we make the difficult decision that we think is best for the organization over the long run?" Berry said.

The Browns will receive a 2027 first-round selection, a 2028 second-round pick, and a 2029 third-round selection alongside Verse. The 25-year-old defensive end was a first-round pick by Los Angeles in 2024 and won Defensive Rookie of the Year honors. He also earned Pro Bowl selection this past season and has recorded 12 career sacks with 22 tackles for loss.

The Rams, who lost to the Seattle Seahawks in last season's NFC championship game, are pursuing another Super Bowl run. Los Angeles is familiar with bold trades, having acquired Matthew Stafford from Detroit in 2021. Stafford led the Rams to a Super Bowl victory in his first season, and won the NFL MVP award last year.

The addition of Garrett gives the Rams a defensive anchor alongside Stafford as they prepare for Super Bowl LXI, which will be played at their home stadium, SoFi Stadium in Inglewood, California.

cards.headline: Giannis Antetokounmpo trade rumors intensify as NBA Finals begin
cards.teaser: The Miami Heat remain at the forefront of trade talks for Milwaukee Bucks star Giannis Antetokounmpo as the NBA Finals tip off.
cards.body:
The Miami Heat have emerged as the leading contender to acquire Giannis Antetokounmpo from the Milwaukee Bucks, according to reports from multiple outlets including The Athletic and Hoops Rumors. The Boston Celtics also remain in discussions as potential suitors for the two-time MVP as trade speculation builds during the NBA Finals.

The timing of the trade rumors coincides with the start of the NBA Finals and the approaching free agency period. Yahoo Sports reported that Antetokounmpo's two biggest trade suitors have been revealed as the deal zone nears. The potential trade would represent one of the most significant player movements in recent NBA history, reshaping the Eastern Conference competitive balance.

cards.headline: World number one Aryna Sabalenka loses French Open quarterfinal
cards.teaser: Aryna Sabalenka's French Open title hopes ended with a quarterfinal defeat to Diana Shnaider.
cards.body:
World number one Aryna Sabalenka crashed out of the French Open quarterfinals in a stunning collapse, losing to 25th seed Diana Shnaider 3-6, 7-5, 6-0. The defeat saw Sabalenka lose 10 consecutive games as her performance deteriorated dramatically through the match.

In her post-match press conference, Sabalenka expressed her distress over the loss, saying she wanted to "quit tennis right now." She acknowledged her severe mental struggles during the match and suggested the roof should have been closed due to windy conditions. The top seed's exit marks one of the worst meltdowns of her career.

cards.headline: SEC and Big Ten oppose congressional college sports bill
cards.teaser: The SEC and Big Ten conferences released a joint statement opposing the Protect College Sports Act, citing critical issues with the proposed legislation.
cards.body:
The Southeastern Conference and Big Ten Conference issued a joint statement announcing their opposition to the Protect College Sports Act currently under consideration in Congress. The two major conferences cited critical issues with the bill that would regulate college athletics.

Former Alabama coach Nick Saban testified before Congress in support of the legislation, asking lawmakers to bring order to college sports. Saban's backing of the Senate bill stands in contrast to the position taken by the two largest and most powerful conferences in college football. USA Today reported that Saban's congressional testimony should worry college sports stakeholders.

cards.headline: Qualifier Maja Chwalinska reaches French Open semifinals
cards.teaser: Maja Chwalinska advanced to her first Grand Slam semifinal after defeating Anna Kalinskaya at the French Open.
cards.body:
Qualifier Maja Chwalinska continued her dream run at the French Open by defeating Anna Kalinskaya to reach the semifinals. The victory marks her first appearance in the final four of a Grand Slam tournament.

Chwalinska's progression through qualifying rounds and into the latter stages of Roland Garros represents one of the standout stories of this year's tournament. She will now compete in the semifinals for a chance to reach the championship match.

cards.headline: New York City reverses ban on Knicks watch party outside Madison Square Garden
cards.teaser: New York City officials reversed a decision that would have prevented fans from gathering outside Madison Square Garden for NBA Finals watch parties.
cards.body:
The city reversed its ban on outdoor watch parties for New York Knicks NBA Finals games outside Madison Square Garden. The decision allows fans to congregate outside the arena to watch the championship series against the San Antonio Spurs.

The reversal comes as ticket prices for Finals games have reached extraordinary levels, with some nosebleed seats priced at $4,000 according to CNN. Madison Square Garden is auctioning celebrity row tickets for Game 3 of the Finals. ABC7 New York compared current prices to historical costs for Knicks games and examined food expenses for watch parties.

cards.headline: Trump says White House UFC arena could become permanent installation
cards.teaser: President Trump compared the temporary UFC arena at the White House to the Eiffel Tower and suggested it might remain in place indefinitely.
cards.body:
President Trump has suggested that the UFC arena constructed at the White House might remain as a permanent structure, likening it to the Eiffel Tower. He indicated the temporary installation built for UFC events could evolve into a lasting feature on the White House grounds.

The Pentagon has distributed memos encouraging military personnel to attend the White House UFC fights.

hero.headline: Disney Sells Super Bowl Ads at $8 Million After Advertiser Pushback on $10 Million Price
hero.body:
Disney has begun selling commercial time for Super Bowl LXI after reducing its asking price from $10 million to $8 million per 30-second spot. The company faced resistance from advertisers over its initial pricing strategy, which required buyers to pay $10 million for both the game spot and an additional $10 million for other inventory tied to its 2027 broadcast.

The media giant has now moved a significant portion of its Super Bowl commercial inventory following the price adjustment. The initial $10 million price tag for a 30-second advertisement represented a premium over previous Super Bowl rates, prompting complaints from potential advertisers before Disney agreed to lower the cost.

Super Bowl LXI is scheduled to air on Disney networks in 2027. The company's decision to bundle Super Bowl commercial slots with other advertising inventory at a combined $20 million total created friction with Madison Avenue buyers, who balked at the required additional spending beyond the game itself.

The adjustment comes as television networks face pressure in the advertising market. Major broadcasters are working to secure commitments from advertisers who have been cutting budgets for traditional programming categories including dramas, comedies, and reality shows. Networks are increasingly relying on sports content to attract advertising dollars as other programming categories see reduced spending.

Disney's revised pricing structure appears to have unlocked advertiser interest after the initial resistance. The $8 million rate for Super Bowl commercials still represents a substantial investment for brands seeking to reach the game's massive audience, which typically draws over 100 million viewers and ranks as the most-watched television event of the year.

cards.headline: Television Networks Push Sports Advertising as Madison Avenue Cuts Programming Budgets
cards.teaser: Major TV networks and streaming platforms are pushing advertisers to spend on sports content while Madison Avenue reduces funding for traditional programming.
cards.body:
Television networks and streaming services are aggressively marketing sports content to advertisers as Madison Avenue reduces spending on traditional programming. Networks are commanding premium advertising rates for sports while cutting budgets for dramas, comedies, and reality shows.

This strategy reflects networks' efforts to stabilize revenue amid shifting viewer behavior and tighter advertiser budgets. Sports programming has become central to networks' upfront negotiations, where they secure advertising commitments from major brands.

cards.headline: Netflix Greenlights Animated Comedy Series Set in Big Box Store
cards.teaser: Netflix has ordered Dealies, an adult animated comedy about employees at a big box retail store.
cards.body:
Netflix has ordered Dealies, a new adult animated comedy series. The show follows a group of employees at a big box store called Dealies, described as a savant salesman, gentle gladiator, quiet virtuoso, summoner of the divine, and the person who hired them.

The series joins Netflix's growing slate of adult animation programming. The streaming platform has been expanding its animated content offerings for adult audiences in recent years.

cards.headline: Emma Roberts Signs With United Talent Agency
cards.teaser: The American Horror Story actress and producer has joined UTA for representation.
cards.body:
Emma Roberts has signed with United Talent Agency for representation. The actress, known for American Horror Story, also runs production company Belletrist, which produced Hulu's Tell Me Lies and Netflix's First Kill.

Tell Me Lies ran for three seasons on Hulu. Roberts is currently serving as executive producer on upcoming projects through her production banner.

cards.headline: Tom Holland Turned Down Saturday Night Live Over Dyslexia Concerns
cards.teaser: The actor declined to host the sketch comedy show due to fears about reading changing cue cards.
cards.body:
Tom Holland turned down an offer to host Saturday Night Live due to concerns about reading cue cards during the live broadcast. The actor cited his dyslexia as the reason for declining the opportunity.

Holland has received widespread praise for openly discussing how his dyslexia influences his professional decisions. His candid approach to the topic has been described as a "powerful" message.

cards.headline: Snap Promotes Anmol Malhotra to Lead Global Content Partnerships
cards.teaser: The 10-year company veteran takes over the role after the previous head left to join Meta.
cards.body:
Snap has promoted Anmol Malhotra to global head of content and partnerships. Malhotra, who has worked at Snap for 10 years, most recently led sports and media partnerships at the company.

He assumes the position after Jim Shepherd, formerly senior director of global content partnerships at Snap, left to join Meta as senior director of content partnerships. Malhotra will oversee content strategy and partnership development across Snap's platform.

cards.headline: New God of War Game to Feature Kratos' Wife as Lead Character
cards.teaser: PlayStation announced the next God of War installment will star Laufey, though some fans have questioned the decision.
cards.body:
PlayStation revealed God of War Laufey during its State of Play showcase, marking a significant shift for the long-running franchise. Developed by Santa Monica Studio, the game will star Laufey, Kratos' wife, as the lead character rather than the series' traditional protagonist. The announcement came as part of a broader slate of upcoming PlayStation titles.

The reveal has sparked mixed reactions among fans regarding the decision to center the narrative on Laufey instead of Kratos. The game is currently in development for PS5, though Sony has not yet announced a release date.

hero.headline: Trump says he will nominate Todd Blanche as attorney general
hero.body:
President Trump indicated Wednesday that he plans to make acting Attorney General Todd Blanche the permanent leader of the Justice Department, though he declined to provide a specific timeline for submitting the nomination to the Senate.

During an appearance on the podcast Pod Force One, Trump expressed confidence in Blanche's performance. "He's a very talented guy. Todd's doing a very good job at DOJ," Trump said when asked about making the position permanent. The president responded affirmatively when directly asked if Blanche would become attorney general, saying "I think he will."

Blanche has served as acting attorney general since Trump took office. Before joining the administration, he worked as a defense attorney and represented Trump in various legal matters. His appointment as a permanent attorney general would require Senate confirmation by the Republican-controlled Senate, which could facilitate the approval process.

The nomination comes as Blanche faces significant legal challenges related to his handling of documents under the Epstein Files Transparency Act. Investigative journalist Katie Phang filed a lawsuit in federal court Monday alleging that Blanche engaged in a "brazen, shocking, and ongoing violation" of the transparency law requiring the Department of Justice to release all government documents about Jeffrey Epstein, the late financier and convicted sex offender.

The lawsuit accuses Blanche of missing statutory deadlines for releasing documents, making improper or excessive redactions, failing to explain redactions as required by law, and withholding or retracting documents after they were released. Congress passed the transparency act in November with a December 19, 2025 deadline for full document release.

Blanche has defended the redactions as necessary to prevent inadvertent identification of Epstein's victims, many of whom are minors, and acknowledged that "mistakes are inevitable." However, critics including House Judiciary Committee Democratic ranking member Jamie Raskin said there were "tons of completely unnecessary redactions" alongside failures to redact victims' names.

The lawsuit seeks to have the court declare the Justice Department in violation of the law, order release of all required documents without unlawful redactions, and appoint an independent special master from outside the department to oversee future compliance.

Additionally, the Justice Department's Office of Inspector General announced last week that it was launching its own audit into the department's compliance with the Epstein Files Transparency Act.

The legal action represents the latest enforcement effort for the transparency law, which was authored by Democratic California Representative Ro Khanna and Republican Kentucky Representative Thomas Massie. A hearing date for Phang's lawsuit has not yet been scheduled.

cards.headline: USAID shutdown linked to increased violence in Africa, study finds
cards.teaser: Research published in Science journal connects the dismantling of the development agency to sharp rises in armed clashes, protests, and riots across the continent.
cards.body:
New research suggests the shutdown of the U.S. Agency for International Development led to sharp increases in violence throughout Africa. A research paper published in the Science journal found that African countries that received the most support from USAID experienced armed clashes, protests, and riots in the months following the agency's dismantling.

The study examined patterns of violence in countries that had previously relied on USAID assistance. Areas that depended heavily on the agency's programs saw notable upticks in civil unrest and armed conflict after operations ceased.

cards.headline: Senate prepares first vote on immigration legislation
cards.teaser: The chamber is set to hold its initial vote on an immigration bill as lawmakers advance new proposals.
cards.body:
The Senate plans to hold its first vote on immigration legislation, marking a significant step forward in the legislative process. The vote represents an attempt by lawmakers to address immigration policy through new proposals.

The timing and specific provisions of the bill were not detailed in available information. The vote will test support for immigration reform measures in the current Senate.

cards.headline: Deb Haaland wins Democratic primary for New Mexico governor
cards.teaser: The former Biden administration official could become the first female Native American governor if elected in November.
cards.body:
Original card text (unchanged)

Deb Haaland won the Democratic primary for governor of New Mexico, setting up a general election race where she could make history. Haaland served as an official in the Biden administration before launching her gubernatorial campaign.

If elected, Haaland would become the first female Native American governor in U.S. history. The general election will take place in November, when she will face the Republican nominee.

---

Note: The source material provided discusses California's governor primary, not New Mexico's. Since it does not contain relevant information about the Deb Haaland story, the original card text is returned unchanged.

cards.headline: Jacqui Irwin advances to general election in California congressional race
cards.teaser: The state assemblymember secured one of the top two spots to compete for the seat being vacated by Rep. Julia Brownley.
cards.body:
California State Assemblymember Jacqui Irwin won the primary for California's 26th Congressional District with 40.09 percent of the vote, securing her spot in the November general election. The seat is opening up as Rep. Julia Brownley, the current representative, is not seeking reelection.

Irwin will face the second-place finisher from the primary in the general election to determine who will represent the district in the House.

cards.headline: Trump suggests Vance and Rubio could run together in 2028
cards.teaser: The president praised both officials but stopped short of endorsing either as his preferred successor.
cards.body:
President Trump suggested Vice President Vance and Secretary of State Marco Rubio should run together on a joint Republican ticket in the 2028 presidential election. Trump made the comments during an episode of The New York Post's Pod Force One podcast released Wednesday.

Trump praised both officials but did not say which one he would prefer to see as his successor. The president called the potential pairing hard to beat in a future election.

cards.headline: Graham Platner cites fundraising and polling after sexting scandal
cards.teaser: The Democratic Senate candidate in Maine released a memo seeking to reassure supporters he can still win despite negative headlines.
cards.body:
Democratic Senate candidate Graham Platner released a memo pointing to his fundraising and poll numbers to argue he can win the Maine Senate race despite a sexting scandal that has generated negative headlines. Platner is challenging longtime Sen. Susan Collins in the general election.

The memo was designed to reassure supporters that the campaign remains viable. Democrats are continuing to support Platner, who is described as a plain-spoken political newcomer. The scandal has prompted questions about whether it will affect his chances in the race.
